strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM-bandwidth bound] The elementwise/layout segment (nchw2nhwc 72us + 2x gn_reduce 98us + gn_apply_nhwc_fast 69us + gn_apply_out 115us ~ 360us of 1897us). Every one of these kernels runs at 84-90% DRAM throughput with lts__t_sector_hit_rate 0.15-3.2%: the same 67MB tensor is streamed from DRAM by 4 consecutive kernels with essentially zero L2 reuse. Convs are already at TF32 roofline.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: L2 cache blocking: run the whole block (transpose -> conv1 -> GN1 stats/apply -> conv2 -> GN2 apply+residual) on batch sub-chunks sized so each intermediate tensor (~16-24MB) stays resident in the ~88MB L2 across the 4-5 kernels that touch it. Since all five kernels are DRAM-bound at peak with ~1-3% L2 hit rate, converting the inter-kernel re-reads (reduce read, apply read, conv2 input read) into L2 hits is the only way to cut bytes; GroupNorm stats are per-(n,group), so batch chunking is exactly equivalent.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. (exact code action) In ModelNew.forward, hoist the weight layout conversions OUT of any loop and compute the chunk size before doing any work:
   xc = x.contiguous(); B,C,H,W = xc.shape; img_bytes = C*H*W*4;
   w1 = conv1_weight.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last); w2 = likewise (once, never inside the loop).
   cap = max(1, min(B, 25_165_824 // max(img_bytes,1)))   # ~24MB per live tensor
   chunk = largest divisor d of B with d <= cap (fallback d=B if cap>=B) -> all chunks share one shape so cudnn.benchmark plans and allocator blocks are reused.
   Additionally enforce conv parallelism: while chunk*H*W < 8192 and chunk < B: chunk *= 2 (keeps >=~170 CTAs per conv launch).
2. (exact code action) Replace the single straight-line body with a chunk loop writing into one preallocated output:
   out = torch.empty_like(xc)
   for n0 in range(0, B, chunk):
       xs = xc.narrow(0, n0, chunk)                      # contiguous NCHW slice
       xh = _ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xs); xl = xh.permute(0,3,1,2)
       o  = F.conv2d(xl, w1, None, 1, 1)                 # channels_last
       _ext.gn_silu_nhwc_(o, norm1_weight, norm1_bias, e, 32)
       o2 = F.conv2d(o, w2, None, 1, 1)
       _ext.gn_silu_add_nchw_out(o2, xs, out.narrow(0,n0,chunk), norm2_weight, norm2_bias, e, 32)
   return out
   If chunk == B this is byte-for-byte the current code path (guaranteed no regression on the 2x64x64 and 1x131x131 shapes).
3. Extension change (minimal): add gn_silu_add_nchw_out(y,res,out,w,b,eps,G) that takes a caller-provided contiguous NCHW destination instead of allocating; body identical to gn_apply_out_kernel launch (out.narrow(0,...) on dim0 is contiguous, so the existing indexing math is unchanged). Keep gn_silu_add_nchw as a thin wrapper for compatibility.
4. Keep ALL device kernels unchanged (same block/grid math, same float4 paths, same fp64 stats combine) — the mechanism is purely working-set scheduling, so per-kernel efficiency and numerics are untouched.
5. Reuse buffers implicitly: because every chunk allocates the same sizes, the caching allocator hands back the same addresses for xh/o/o2 each iteration, so chunk k+1's writes land on the same L2 lines as chunk k (no address aliasing hazard: xs and out slices are disjoint tensors).
6. Correctness guard: GroupNorm statistics are computed per (n, group), so per-chunk stats == full-batch stats exactly; compute_stats already recomputes nch/chunk from HW for any H*W (odd 17161 included). Assert res.sizes()==y.sizes() and out.is_contiguous() in the new binding.
7. Tuning: expose the 24MB constant as a module-level _L2_TARGET_BYTES; if measured L2 is smaller, lower to 16MB. Try cap targets {16MB, 24MB, 32MB} once offline and keep the best geometric-mean setting.
8. Verify with NCU that lts__t_sector_hit_rate of gn_reduce_kernel / gn_apply_nhwc_fast / gn_apply_out_kernel rises well above 40% and their durations drop; verify conv kernel names/tile sizes are unchanged (still cutlass tf32 nhwc fprop) so the mainloop stays vendor-optimal.

strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM-latency/uncoalesced-request bound] gn_reduce_kernel (2 launches/iter, 2x49.5us = 99us, the largest non-conv aggregate after the already-saturated apply kernels). It streams 67MB read-only at only 1.385 TB/s (78.5% DRAM) versus 86-90% for its neighbours, because its thread->data map (g = tid%32, float4 at c=g*8+4j) splits every 32B sector across two separate load instructions: 2,146,304 excessive sectors (50%), 92.4% long-scoreboard stalls, IPC 0.21.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: mem_vectorize via warp remapping: give each warp 32 *consecutive* float4 lanes of the NHWC channel row (512B fully-used per request) instead of the group-strided g=tid%G map, and unroll 4 independent pixel rows per thread to raise memory-level parallelism. Each thread then owns a fixed group id (lane*4/CPG), so only the block-level reduction changes. Justified by E1 (92.4% long-scoreboard + 50% excessive sectors + sub-peak 78.5% DRAM on a pure streaming read) and E2 (same bytes, half the sector requests).
strategy.modification_plan:
Checklist (all inside gn_reduce_kernel + its host launcher; every other kernel byte-identical):
1. REPLACE the mapping in gn_reduce_kernel. Delete `int g = tid % G; int dp = tid / G;` and the inner `for (j=0..nv)` float4 loop. Use instead: `const int C4 = C>>2; const int lane = tid % C4; const int row = tid / C4; const int rows = blockDim.x / C4;` and `const float4* v4 = reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(y) + (size_t)n*HW*C4;` with the load `v4[(size_t)p*C4 + lane]`. Consecutive tids now read consecutive float4s => a warp covers 32*16B = 512B contiguous, every 32B sector 100% used (2.15M excessive sectors -> 0). Each thread's group is compile-time-fixed: `const int g = (lane*4)/CPG;` (C=256, G=32, CPG=8 => 2 lanes per group), so one scalar (s,q) accumulator per thread suffices.
2. 4-WAY UNROLLED STREAM for MLP: `long p = pstart + row; for (; p + 3L*rows < pend; p += 4L*rows) { float4 a=v4[(p)*C4+lane], b=v4[(p+rows)*C4+lane], c=v4[(p+2*rows)*C4+lane], d=v4[(p+3*rows)*C4+lane]; accumulate all four; } for (; p < pend; p += rows) { single load; }` — 4 loads in flight per thread instead of 1, directly attacking the 92.4% long-scoreboard stall.
3. NEW BLOCK REDUCTION (two stages, no divergence): stage A, tree over the `row` dimension with stride `C4` (rows is a power of two): `for (int st=rows>>1; st>0; st>>=1){ if(row<st){ s_s[tid]+=s_s[tid+st*C4]; s_q[tid]+=s_q[tid+st*C4];} __syncthreads(); }`. Stage B, threads with row==0 hold one partial per lane; fold the `CPG/4` lanes belonging to the same group: `int LPG = CPG>>2; if(row==0){ if(lane % LPG == 0){ float S=0,Q=0; for(int k=0;k<LPG;k++){S+=s_s[lane+k];Q+=s_q[lane+k];} psum[(size_t)(n*G+g)*nch+blockIdx.x]=(double)S; psq[...]=(double)Q; } }`.
4. HOST LAUNCHER (compute_stats): replace `ppb` with `rows`. Require the fast path only when `C%4==0 && CPG%4==0 && C4<=256`; pick `rows = max(1, min(8, 256/C4))` rounded down to a power of two, `block = C4*rows` (=256 for C=256). Otherwise launch the existing scalar kernel unchanged (generic fallback preserved).
5. TAIL SAFETY (regression guard from history): keep the existing sequence `chunk = ceil(HW/nch); chunk = align_up(chunk, rows); nch = ceil(HW/chunk);` so grid coverage is exact for odd HW (131x131 = 17161). A block whose [pstart,pend) is empty must still write zeros to its psum/psq slot — keep the unconditional store in stage B so gn_finalize never reads uninitialised memory.
6. Shared memory stays `2*block*sizeof(float)` = 2KB; no smem tiling added, no occupancy change (regs ~40 -> unchanged target).
7. Numerics: still fp32 per-thread accumulation combined in fp64 by gn_finalize; only the summation order changes, well inside max_atol 0.0028. No dtype change anywhere.
8. Validate on all four shapes (8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) that mean/rstd match the current kernel bitwise-approximately (<1e-6 rel) before timing.
strategy.evidence: gn_reduce_kernel: gpu__time_duration.avg = 49,536 ns x2 launches/iter (~99us of the 365us non-conv segment); gpu__dram_throughput = 78.52% vs 86.2/86.2/89.7% for nchw2nhwc/apply_fast/apply_out; UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule: 2,146,304 excessive sectors = 50% of 4,259,840; smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard = 92.37% at IPC 0.21 with 94.3% achieved occupancy. Root cause: g=tid%G makes each thread's two float4 loads land 32B apart, so every load instruction requests 32 sectors but uses only 16B of each (l1tex hit 49.23% is exactly the second half arriving later), halving effective DRAM efficiency on a pure-read stream. Refuting the alternative 'gn_apply_out is the bottleneck': it moves 201MB in 115.5us = 1.74 TB/s = 97% of the 1792 GB/s peak, and the two convs run 154.6 GFLOP in ~1533us = 100.9 TFLOPS = 96% of TF32 peak — neither has headroom.

strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM-bandwidth/traffic bound] Composite GroupNorm-2 segment: gn_reduce (48.9us) + gn_finalize (4.6us) + gn_apply_out_kernel (115.9us, hottest non-conv kernel). Each already runs at 84-89% DRAM peak, but lts__t_sector_hit_rate is 3.2%/1.05%: the same 67MB conv output is streamed from DRAM twice because stats and apply are separate launches whose traversal orders do not overlap in L2.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Grid-sync kernel fusion: merge reduce+finalize+apply of each GroupNorm into ONE persistent cooperative kernel whose phase-2 blocks re-touch exactly the pixel range they read in phase-1, so the second read of the 67MB tensor hits L2 instead of DRAM. Justified by E1/E2: kernels are at DRAM roofline (88.9%) so only byte removal helps; gn_apply_nhwc_fast already shows 50.4% L2 hit when it follows the reduce, proving the reuse is capturable. Also removes 4 launches/forward (helps small shape).
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Replace the 3-launch GN sequence (gn_reduce -> gn_finalize -> apply) with ONE persistent kernel per GroupNorm: `gn_fused_inplace` (GN1, NHWC in-place + SiLU) and `gn_fused_out` (GN2, +residual + NHWC->NCHW). Host side: grid = min(numSMs * cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(kernel,256,smem), ceil(HW/PIX_TILE)*B); launch with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel; keep the existing 3-kernel path as a fallback if the cooperative launch returns any error or if the required grid exceeds residency.
2. Data-locality rule (the actual saving): partition work ONLY over (n, pixel-chunk); every block owns the SAME (n, pixel range) in phase 1 and phase 2, and covers ALL 256 channels of those pixels in both phases. Traverse chunks with a grid-stride loop in identical order in both phases, so phase-2 loads reference the most-recently-filled L2 lines.
3. Phase 1 (stats): each block loops its chunks, reads NHWC float4 rows exactly as today's gn_reduce (keep current access pattern; do NOT change vector width), accumulates fp32 per-thread s/q, block-reduces in shared memory, writes fp64 partials to psum/psq[block][n][g].
4. Barrier A: cooperative_groups::this_grid().sync(). Add `-rdc=true` to extra_cuda_cflags (fallback: manual arrive-and-wait barrier on an int counter allocated with torch::zeros and __threadfence + volatile spin).
5. Finalize inside the kernel: blocks with blockIdx.x < B*G each read gridDim.x partial pairs (<=~8KB) and compute mean/rstd into small global arrays (fp64 combine, unchanged math). Barrier B: grid sync again.
6. Phase 2 (apply), GN1 variant: identical to gn_apply_nhwc_fast body (float4, precomputed a=r*w, d=b-m*a, FMA + SiLU), but iterating the block's OWN chunk list from step 2, in-place.
7. Phase 2, GN2 variant (replaces gn_apply_out_kernel): for each owned 32-pixel chunk, loop ct=0..C/32-1: load y[(p0+ty+i)*C + c0+tx] (32 contiguous floats/warp, same lines phase 1 touched), apply (v-mean)*rstd*w[c]+b[c] then SiLU, stage into __shared__ float tile[32][33] (bytes_per_block = 32*33*4 = 4224 B, one buffer, far below the 99KB/block limit, reused across ct so smem is constant), __syncthreads(), then write out[((n*C)+c)*HW + p] = tile[tx][ty+i] + res[same offset] with coalesced 32-pixel NCHW stores. Because the block now sweeps all 256 channels of its pixel chunk instead of one 32-channel slice, the y reads are contiguous whole-pixel rows and reuse the phase-1 L2 residency (today's 1.05% hit rate).
8. Tail handling: guards `p < HW` and `c < C` retained; grid-stride chunk loop makes coverage correct for odd HW (131x131 -> HW=17161) and for B=1; partial arrays sized gridDim.x*B*G, fully written by every block (no unwritten tail).
9. Numerics unchanged: fp32 storage, fp32 per-thread accumulation, fp64 combine, same eps/rstd formula, TF32 convs untouched (F.conv2d channels_last kept as the mainloop).
10. Keep nchw2nhwc_kernel and both cuDNN convs exactly as-is; launch count per forward drops from ~20 to ~16.
11. Validate: max_atol <= tolerance on all four shapes; verify the conv engine selection (cutlass tf32 nhwc fprop) is unchanged in nsys; if the cooperative grid is smaller than 2 waves for the large shape, cap PIX_TILE so each block still gets >=2 chunks.

strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM-bound elementwise segment serialized behind compute-bound convs] Hottest non-removable kernel gn_apply_out_kernel: 123.4us at 89.6% DRAM but only 34.9% SM throughput; with gn_reduce (2x49.6us, 4.8% SM) and gn_apply_nhwc_fast (67.2us, 25.6% SM) the elementwise segment is ~371us of 1897us. Meanwhile the two cuDNN convs run ~1.53ms at ~101 TFLOPS (96% of TF32 peak) using only ~10-15% of DRAM bandwidth. The two phases never overlap.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Stream pipelining over the batch: samples are fully independent end-to-end (conv is per-sample; GroupNorm stats are per-(n,group)), so shard N into 2-4 shards and run each shard's transpose->conv1->GN1->conv2->GN2 chain on its own CUDA stream. Memory-bound kernels (89% DRAM / 25-35% SM) then co-reside with tensor-core convs (96% FLOP / ~15% DRAM), hiding most of the 371us elementwise time. Combined demand 871MB/1.53ms = 570 GB/s, far below 1792 GB/s, so overlap is bandwidth-feasible.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Extension change (enables in-place shard writes): add `gn_silu_add_nchw_out(y,res,out,w,b,eps,G)` that takes a pre-allocated NCHW destination instead of calling torch::empty; keep the existing wrapper delegating to it. Slices out[n0:n1] of a contiguous NCHW tensor are contiguous, so TORCH_CHECK(out.is_contiguous()) still holds.
2. Add a grid-stride outer loop over pixel-tiles in nchw2nhwc_kernel and gn_apply_out_kernel (`for (long bx=blockIdx.x; bx<ntx; bx+=gridDim.x)` with p0=bx*TILE) and cap grid.x at ~2 waves (min(ntx, 2*170*blocksPerSM)); this lets conv CTAs from another stream co-reside instead of a 16384-block grid monopolizing every SM. Correctness for odd HW is unchanged (bounds checks retained).
3. Python: module-level lazy pool `_STREAMS = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(4)]` created on first use, reused across calls (no per-call stream creation).
4. In forward, first compute the shared read-only tensors on the current stream: xc = x.contiguous(), w1/w2 channels_last copies, contiguous norm params. Record `ev0 = torch.cuda.Event(); ev0.record()`.
5. Gate: `nsh = 1 if (B < 2 or B*H*W < 2*8192) else min(B, 4)`; if nsh==1 execute exactly today's single-stream path (guarantees 1x256x131x131 and the tiny shape cannot regress).
6. Allocate the full output once on the current stream: `out = torch.empty(B,C,H,W, ...)` (or torch.empty_like(xc)).
7. Shard loop i in range(nsh): n0,n1 = even split of B; `with torch.cuda.stream(_STREAMS[i]):` `_STREAMS[i].wait_event(ev0)`; run the existing chain on the contiguous view xs = xc[n0:n1]: xh=_ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xs); xl=xh.permute(0,3,1,2); o=F.conv2d(xl,w1,None,1,1) (+channels_last guard); _ext.gn_silu_nhwc_(o,...); o2=F.conv2d(o,w2,None,1,1); `_ext.gn_silu_add_nchw_out(o2, xs, out[n0:n1], norm2_w, norm2_b, eps, 32)`. All temporaries (xh, o, o2, GN partial buffers) are allocated inside the stream context so the caching allocator tags them correctly.
8. Cross-stream safety: call `t.record_stream(_STREAMS[i])` for xc, w1, w2, norm params and out (tensors allocated on the current stream but consumed on side streams). After the loop, for each used stream record an event and `torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_event(ev_i)` so the returned tensor is ordered on the caller's stream.
9. Keep eps extraction (`eps.item()`) before the stream loop to avoid a sync inside the pipeline.
10. Validate: output values bit-identical to the current path (per-sample GN stats, same kernels, same order within a shard) on all four shapes; verify with nsys that conv CTAs and gn_* CTAs are resident concurrently and that wall time drops.

Every custom kernel is already at 84-90% DRAM peak (gn_apply_out: 201 MB in 116 us = 1.73 TB/s = 97% of 1792 GB/s), so the elementwise segment holds <30 us of headroom; only the conv mainloop has real time left.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Switch the conv mainloop algorithm: call cuDNN directly inside the extension and select CUDNN_CONVOLUTION_FWD_ALGO_WINOGRAD_NONFUSED (fp32 NCHW, stride 1, 3x3) instead of PyTorch's NHWC implicit-GEMM. Winograd F(2x2,3x3) is an exact algebraic rewrite that cuts multiplies 2.25x (154.6 GFLOP -> ~68.7 GFLOP of tile MACs). On GeForce Blackwell FP32 CUDA-core rate equals TF32 tensor rate (104.8 TFLOPS), so fewer multiplies translates directly into less time. Vendor library only; dtype unchanged (fp32/TF32).

3. Because Winograd-nonfused requires NCHW, add the two NCHW post-op kernels so the whole block stays NCHW and BOTH layout transposes (`nchw2nhwc_kernel`, 72 us, and the smem transpose inside `gn_apply_out_kernel`) disappear:
   a. `gn_reduce_nchw`: grid=(nch, B*G), each block walks the CPG=8 contiguous channel planes of its group over a chunk of HW; threads cover contiguous W (fully coalesced, no smem staging), `float4` loads when HW%4==0 and a scalar tail loop otherwise (needed for HW=17161); per-thread fp32 s/q, block reduce in 2 KB smem, write partials; reuse existing `gn_finalize_kernel` unchanged (chunk/nch recompute logic kept verbatim so odd HW is fully covered).
   b. `gn_apply_nchw`: one block per (n,c) row-chunk so `a = rstd[n*G+c/CPG]*w[c]`, `d = b[c] - mean*a` are computed ONCE per block and applied with FMA: `out = silu(v*a + d)` for GN1 (in place) and `out = silu(v*a+d) + res` for GN2 (res read is contiguous NCHW, same address as out). float4 when HW%4==0 + scalar tail.
4. Path selection (no regression risk): static cache keyed by (B,C,H,W). On first call for a shape, time (cudaEvent, 2 warm + 3 timed iters) (i) the existing channels_last path, (ii) the new NCHW-Winograd path; store the winner and use it thereafter. Any cuDNN failure (NOT_SUPPORTED on sm_120) permanently selects the existing path, so worst case is today's performance.
5. Keep both weight staging variants: NCHW path uses `conv1_weight`/`conv2_weight` as-is (already contiguous NCHW) — this also removes the two channels_last weight copies.
6. Output: NCHW path returns the `gn_apply_nchw` output tensor directly (already contiguous NCHW) — no final transpose.

METHOD STEPS (why this is the single mechanism)
- Only the algorithm used by the conv mainloop changes: direct-implicit-GEMM (9 multiplies/output/channel) -> Winograd F(2x2,3x3) (4 multiplies/output/channel), an exact algebraic transform; layout/GN kernels are enabling plumbing, not a second optimisation.
- dtype is untouched: fp32 storage, fp32/TF32 math, fp32 reductions with fp64 finalize, as today.
- Validate max_atol on all four shapes; if Winograd's error exceeds tolerance on any shape, the selector must reject it for that shape (add an atol self-check against the fallback path during the one-time probe).
strategy.evidence: Numeric: profiled custom kernels total 72.8+2x49.6+68.1+116.7+2x4.4 = 365 us of a 1897 us forward -> convs are ~1.53 ms (80%); gn_apply_out moves 201 MB in 116.7 us = 1.73 TB/s = 97% of the 1792 GB/s peak (gpu__dram_throughput 88-89.5%), and nchw2nhwc runs 1.84 TB/s at 86.3% DRAM. Root cause: with every memory-side kernel already at DRAM roofline, the only remaining time is arithmetic in the 3x3 convs (154.6 GFLOP at ~101 TFLOPS), and Winograd removes 55% of those multiplies. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_apply_out/gn_reduce is the bottleneck': four prior rounds of L2 blocking, vectorisation, grid-sync fusion and stream overlap each landed 1.085-1.130 geomean versus the current 1.1235 baseline, i.e. the elementwise segment is exhausted (<30 us theoretical headroom, 1.6% of forward).
strategy.expected_metric_change: (1) Conv segment duration 1.53 ms -> 1.0-1.25 ms; the profile should show cudnn winograd_nonfused kernels replacing sm80_xmma/cutlass tf32 fprop, with sm__throughput staying >70% and gpu__dram_throughput on conv staying low (<25%). (2) nchw2nhwc_kernel (72.8 us) and the smem-transpose epilogue disappear: kernels/iteration 9 -> 7, elementwise DRAM traffic 603 MB -> ~470 MB, so the non-conv segment drops 365 us -> ~270 us; gn_apply_nchw should reach >=85% gpu__dram_throughput like today's kernels. Anti-regression: one-time per-shape A/B timing with permanent fallback to the current channels_last path means no shape (2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) can be slower than today; Winograd workspace capped at 1 GB; scalar tail loops keep HW=17161 exact; max_atol must stay <= 0.0027/0.0028/0.0030/0.0029 per shape or the probe rejects Winograd.
